<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The plan starts by keeping the existing `tsconfig.json` as the base for package source compilation.

A separate tsconfig will handle scripts/ and tests/. `bun run typecheck` will cover all directories. The preferred approach uses project references to avoid breaking package declaration emit. Two patterns are under consideration: separate tsconfig files per directory, or a single noEmit check file.

The `typecheck` command currently runs `bunx tsgo --noEmit` against `tsconfig.json`, which only covers `src`. `build:declaration` already uses `tsconfig.types.json`. The concrete plan is to create `tsconfig.scripts.json` and `tsconfig.tests.json` extending the base `tsconfig.json`, then update the `typecheck` script to run all three configs.

Project references would break the current `rootDir: ./src` setting in `tsconfig.json`, so that path is abandoned. The safer route is to leave `tsconfig.json` untouched for package emit and IDE safety, then create a separate `tsconfig.check.json` that extends the base and includes `scripts/` and `tests/` with `noEmit`. A shared `tsconfig.base.json` is also being considered to avoid duplicating common compiler options.

The single-check-config option is now favored over separate tsconfigs. `tsconfig.check.json` would extend `tsconfig.json` and set `rootDir` to `"."` since `scripts/` and `tests/` sit outside `src/`. It would include all three directories with `noEmit` and disabled declarations. The `typecheck` script would run `tsgo` against each config sequentially.

The next step is to probe for type errors by running a check config. Scripts may need different settings, so the first pass will reveal what actually breaks.
</details></think>
